nodes.summary: Let $k$ and $n$ be natural numbers, write $n^{\overline{k}} = n (n + 1) \cdots (n + k - 1)$ for the rising factorial, and let $r = \lfloor (k^2 - 4k + 6)/4 \rfloor$ if $k$ is even and $r = \lfloor (k^2 - 6k + 11)/4 \rfloor$ if $k$ is odd. If $n \ge r$, then $(n + \lfloor k/2 \rfloor - 1)^k \le n^{\overline{k}} \le (n + \lfloor k/2 \rfloor)^k$.
nodes.title: Rising factorial between consecutive $k$-th powers

nodes.summary: Sequences $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ form a complementary pair determined by this equation when they form a complementary pair (both strictly increasing with positive terms, and every positive integer is a term of exactly one of them) and they satisfy $b_0 = 1$ and $a_n = b_{2n} + b_{4n}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Complementary pair determined by $a_n = b_{2n} + b_{4n}$

nodes.summary: Sequences $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ form a complementary pair determined by this equation with natural-number parameters $h$ and $k$ when they form a complementary pair (both strictly increasing with positive terms, and every positive integer is a term of exactly one of them), $h \ge 2$, $k \ge 2$, $b_0 = 1$, and $a_n = b_{hn} + b_{khn}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Complementary pair determined by $a_n = b_{hn} + b_{khn}$

nodes.summary: Sequences $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ form a complementary pair determined by this equation when they form a complementary pair (both strictly increasing with positive terms, and every positive integer is a term of exactly one of them) and they satisfy $b_0 = 1$ and $a_n = b_{2n} + b_{4n} + 1$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Complementary pair determined by $a_n = b_{2n} + b_{4n} + 1$

nodes.summary: Two sequences $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, indexed from $0$, form a complementary pair when all their terms are positive, both are strictly increasing, no term of $a$ equals a term of $b$, and every positive integer is a term of $a$ or a term of $b$. In particular, the ranges of $a$ and $b$ partition the positive integers.
nodes.title: Complementary pair of sequences

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 3$; the centered $k$-gonal numbers are $k j (j + 1)/2 + 1$ for $j \ge 0$. For $n \ge 1$ let $a(n)$ be the $n$-th nonnegative integer that is not a centered $k$-gonal number (so $a(1) = 0$), and let $s = \lfloor \sqrt{2n/k} \rfloor$. Then $a(n) = n + s$ if $k s (s + 1) < 2(n + s - 1)$, and $a(n) = n + s - 1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Non-centered polygonal numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$. For $n \ge 1$ let $a(n)$ be the $n$-th positive integer that is not of the form $m + \sum_{i=1}^m i^k$ with $m \ge 1$, and let $h = \lfloor ((k + 1) n)^{1/(k+1)} \rfloor$. Then $a(n) = n + h - 1$ if $n \le \sum_{i=1}^h i^k$, and $a(n) = n + h$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Integers not of the form $m + 1^k + \cdots + m^k$

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(1) \ge 1$ and $f(m + 1) \ge f(m) + m$ for all $m \ge 1$, and for $n \ge 1$ let $f_P(n)$ be the $n$-th positive integer that is not a value $f(m)$ with $m \ge 1$. Let $\alpha : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $f(m - 1) \le \alpha(m) \le f(m)$ for all $m \ge 2$, and let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $h(n) \ge 1$ and $\alpha(h(n)) \le n < \alpha(h(n) + 1)$…
nodes.title: Interleaving formula when $f(m) - \alpha(m) \ge m$

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(1) \ge 1$ and $f(m + 1) \ge f(m) + m$ for all $m \ge 1$, and for $n \ge 1$ let $f_P(n)$ be the $n$-th positive integer that is not a value $f(m)$ with $m \ge 1$. Let $\alpha : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $f(m - 1) \le \alpha(m) \le f(m)$ for all $m \ge 2$, and let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $h(n) \ge 1$ and $\alpha(h(n)) \le n < \alpha(h(n) + 1)$…
nodes.title: Interleaving formula when $f(m) - \alpha(m) < m$

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(1) \ge 1$ and $f(m + 1) \ge f(m) + m$ for all $m \ge 1$, and for $n \ge 1$ let $f_P(n)$ be the $n$-th positive integer that is not a value $f(m)$ with $m \ge 1$. Let $\alpha : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfy $f(m - 1) \le \alpha(m) \le f(m)$ for all $m \ge 2$, and let $h : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $h(n) \ge 1$ and $\alpha(h(n)) \le n < \alpha(h(n) + 1)$…
nodes.title: Complementary sequences from an interleaving function

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(1) \ge 1$ and $f(m + 1) \ge f(m) + m$ for all $m \ge 1$, let $C(x)$ be the number of $m$ with $1 \le m \le x$ and $f(m) \le x$, and for $n \ge 1$ let $f_P(n)$ be the $n$-th positive integer that is not a value $f(m)$ with $m \ge 1$. Then for every $n \ge 1$, $f_P(n) = n + C(n) + 1$ if $f(C(n) + 1) \le n + C(n)$, and $f_P(n) = n + C(n)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Complementary sequences from one evaluation of the counting function

nodes.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy $f(1) \ge 1$ and $f(m + 1) \ge f(m) + m$ for all $m \ge 1$, let $C(x)$ be the number of $m$ with $1 \le m \le x$ and $f(m) \le x$, and for $n \ge 1$ let $f_P(n)$ be the $n$-th positive integer that is not a value $f(m)$ with $m \ge 1$. Then $f_P(n) = n + C(n + C(n))$ for every $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Complementary sequences in two Lambek–Moser steps

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 3$; the $k$-gonal numbers are $(k - 2) j (j - 1)/2 + j$ for $j \ge 1$. For every $n \ge 1$, the $n$-th positive integer that is not a $k$-gonal number equals $n + \lfloor \sqrt{(2n - 2 + \lfloor (k + 1)/4 \rfloor)/(k - 2)} + 1/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Rounding formula for the non-$k$-gonal numbers, every $k \ge 3$

nodes.summary: Let $3 \le k \le 10$; the $k$-gonal numbers are $(k - 2) j (j - 1)/2 + j$ for $j \ge 1$. For every $n \ge 1$, the $n$-th positive integer that is not a $k$-gonal number equals $n + \lfloor \sqrt{2n/(k - 2)} + 1/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Rounding formula for the non-$k$-gonal numbers, $3 \le k \le 10$

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 3$, let $r$ be a real number with $-1 \le r \le k - 4$, and for $j \ge 1$ let $T(k, j) = (k - 2) j (j - 1)/2 + j$ be the $k$-gonal numbers. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $s = \lfloor \sqrt{(2n + r)/(k - 2)} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not of the form $T(k, j)$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $n + s + 1$ if $(k - 2) s (s + 1) < 2n$, and $n + s$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Shifted formula for the non-polygonal numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k \ge 3$, and for $j \ge 1$ let $T(k, j) = (k - 2) j (j - 1)/2 + j$ be the $k$-gonal numbers. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $s = \lfloor \sqrt{2n/(k - 2)} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not of the form $T(k, j)$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $n + s + 1$ if $(k - 2) s (s + 1) < 2n$, and $n + s$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Formula for the non-polygonal numbers

nodes.summary: Let $3 \le k \le 8$, and for $j \ge 1$ let $P(k, j) = j (j + 1) ((k - 2) j - (k - 5))/6$ be the $k$-gonal pyramidal numbers. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $s = \lfloor \sqrt[3]{6n/(k - 2)} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not of the form $P(k, j)$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $n + s - 1$ if $6n \le s (s - 1) (s (k - 2) + k + 1)$, and $n + s$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Two-case formula for the non-pyramidal numbers when $k \le 8$

nodes.summary: Let $3 \le k \le 5$, and for $j \ge 1$ let $P(k, j) = j (j + 1) ((k - 2) j - (k - 5))/6$ be the $k$-gonal pyramidal numbers. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $s = \lfloor \sqrt[3]{6n/(k - 2)} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not of the form $P(k, j)$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $n + s - 1$ if $6n \le s (s - 1) (s (k - 2) + k + 1)$, and $n + s$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Two-case formula for the non-pyramidal numbers when $k \le 5$

nodes.summary: Let $3 \le k \le 8$, and for $j \ge 1$ let $P(k, j) = j (j + 1) ((k - 2) j - (k - 5))/6$ be the $k$-gonal pyramidal numbers. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $s = \lfloor \sqrt[3]{6n/(k - 2)} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not of the form $P(k, j)$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $n + s + 1$ if $6n \ge s^3 (k - 2) + 3 s^2 (k - 1) + s (2k - 1) + 6$; otherwise it equals $n + s - 1$ if…
nodes.title: Formula for the non-pyramidal numbers

nodes.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $s = \lfloor \sqrt{2n/3} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not a second pentagonal number $(3j^2 + j)/2$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $n + s + 1$ if $s (3s + 5) + 4 \le 2n$, and $n + s$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Formula for the non-second-pentagonal numbers

nodes.summary: Let $k > 5$, and for $j \ge 1$ let $S(k, j) = ((k - 2) j^2 + (k - 4) j)/2$ be the second $k$-gonal numbers. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $s = \lfloor \sqrt{2n/(k - 2)} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not of the form $S(k, j)$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $n + s$ if $(k - 2) s (s + 1) < 2n + 4s$, and $n + s - 1$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Formula for the non-second-polygonal numbers

nodes.summary: Let $1 < k \le 15$. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $R = \lfloor (k!\, n)^{1/k} \rfloor$ and let $t = n + R - \lfloor k/2 \rfloor$, an integer. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not a $k$-simplex number $\binom{j + k - 1}{k}$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $t + 2$ if $\binom{R + \lceil k/2 \rceil + 1}{k} \le t + 1$; otherwise it equals $t$ if $t < \binom{R + \lceil k/2 \rceil}{k}$, and $t + 1$ if not.
nodes.title: Formula for the non-simplex numbers when $k \le 15$

nodes.summary: Let $k$ satisfy $1 < k \le 5$, $k = 7$ or $k = 9$. For every integer $n \ge 1$, put $R = \lfloor (k!\, n)^{1/k} \rfloor$ and let $t = n + R - \lfloor k/2 \rfloor$, an integer. Then the $n$-th positive integer that is not a $k$-simplex number $\binom{j + k - 1}{k}$ with $j \ge 1$ equals $t + 2$ if $\binom{R + \lceil k/2 \rceil + 1}{k} \le t + 1$; otherwise it equals $t$ if $t < \binom{R + \lceil k/2 \rceil}{k}$, and…
nodes.title: Formula for the non-simplex numbers

nodes.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the $n$-th positive integer that is not a perfect square is $n + \lfloor \sqrt{n} + 1/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Formula for the non-square numbers

nodes.summary: The smallest positive integer that is not the square of a positive integer is $2$; that is, the first non-value of $m \mapsto m^2$ is $2$.
nodes.title: The first non-square

nodes.summary: The second smallest positive integer that is not the square of a positive integer is $3$; that is, the second non-value of $m \mapsto m^2$ is $3$.
nodes.title: The second non-square

nodes.summary: Let $k > 1$ and $n \ge 1$ be integers, and let $h = \lfloor ((k+1)n)^{1/(k+1)} \rfloor$. Then the $n$-th smallest positive integer that is not of the form $\sum_{i=1}^{j} i^k$ with $j \ge 1$ is $n + h - 1$ if $n \le \sum_{i=1}^{h} (i^k - 1)$, and $n + h$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Integers missed by the sums $1^k + \dots + j^k$

nodes.summary: For every integer $n \ge 1$, the $n$-th smallest positive integer that is not a triangular number $j(j+1)/2$ with $j \ge 1$ is $n + \lfloor \sqrt{2n} + 1/2 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Formula for the $n$-th non-triangular number

nodes.summary: For $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and $n \ge 1$, the $n$-th non-value of $f$ is the $n$-th smallest positive integer that is not of the form $f(m)$ with $m \ge 1$, or $0$ if fewer than $n$ such integers exist. At $n = 0$ it takes the same value as at $n = 1$.
nodes.title: The $n$-th non-value of a sequence

nodes.summary: Sequences $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy this equation when $b_0 = 1$ and $a_n = b_{2n} + b_{4n}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The subsequence-sum equation $a_n = b_{2n} + b_{4n}$

nodes.summary: Sequences $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and natural numbers $h$ and $k$ satisfy the parametrized subsequence-sum equation when $h \ge 2$, $k \ge 2$, $b_0 = 1$, and $a_n = b_{hn} + b_{khn}$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The subsequence-sum equation $a_n = b_{hn} + b_{khn}$

nodes.summary: Sequences $a, b : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ satisfy this equation when $b_0 = 1$ and $a_n = b_{2n} + b_{4n} + 1$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: The subsequence-sum equation $a_n = b_{2n} + b_{4n} + 1$

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
